title.zh: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬
title.en: Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian
title.raw: 卷六十五 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬 Volume 65 Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬

translations.literal: Biographies 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, and Shen Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, and Shen Tian.

sentences.zh: 吉翰，字休文，馮翊池陽人也。

translations.literal: Ji Han, courtesy name Xiuwen, was a native of Chiyang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, whose courtesy name was Xiuwen, came from Chiyang in Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為龍驤將軍道憐參軍，隨府轉征虜左軍參軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was a staff officer under General of the Dragon Cavalry Liu Daolian; with the headquarters he was transferred to Left Army Staff Officer of the Expeditionary Force, then Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a staff officer under Liu Daolian, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and moved with the headquarters to become left-army staff officer for the expeditionary command and then Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 隨道憐北征廣固，賜爵建城縣五等男。

translations.literal: Following Daolian on the northern campaign to Guanggu, he was granted the fifth-rank noble title of Baron of Jiancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Daolian on the northern campaign against Guanggu and was ennobled as fifth-rank Baron of Jiancheng County.

sentences.zh: 轉道憐驃騎中兵參軍，從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Army Staff Officer under Daolian's Rapid Cavalry command and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made central army staff officer on Daolian's Rapid Cavalry staff and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 為將佐十餘年，清謹剛正，甚為高祖所知賞。

translations.literal: Serving as a military aide for more than ten years, he was pure, careful, and upright by nature, and was greatly known and rewarded by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years as a military aide he was scrupulous and upright, and Emperor Gaozu came to know and esteem him highly.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，轉道憐太尉司馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Grand Marshal Staff Officer under Daolian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3 (422) he became staff officer to Daolian as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 時太祖經略河南，以翰為持節、監司、雍、并三州諸軍事、司州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wen was planning operations in Henan and appointed Han Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing provinces, and Inspector of Si Province, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was pressing his strategy south of the Yellow River, he appointed Han Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Bing provinces, and Inspector of Si Province, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 會前鋒諸軍到彥之等敗退，明年，復為司徒司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the vanguard armies under Dao Yanzhi and others were defeated and withdrew, the next year he was again made Grand Minister of State Staff Officer, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the vanguard under Dao Yanzhi and others was beaten and forced to retreat, the following year he was again made staff officer to the Grand Minister of State, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其年，又假節、監徐、兗二州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was also given acting Bearer of the Staff, supervision of military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, and the post of Inspector of Xu Province, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was also given acting Bearer of the Staff, supervision of military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, and the post of Inspector of Xu Province, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時有死罪囚，典籤意欲活之，因翰入關齎呈其事。

translations.literal: At the time there was a prisoner condemned to death; the clerk in charge wished to spare him and, when Han entered the pass, had the matter presented to him.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a prisoner under sentence of death; the clerk in charge hoped to save him and, when Han entered the pass, had the petition brought to him.

sentences.zh: 翰省訖，語「今且去，明可便呈」。

translations.literal: When Han had reviewed it he said, "Go for now; you may present it tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Han read it through and said, "Leave for now; you may bring it in tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 明旦，典籤不敢復入，呼之乃來。

translations.literal: The next morning the clerk did not dare enter again and came only when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the clerk did not dare come in again and appeared only when called.

sentences.zh: 取昨所呈事視訖，謂之曰：「卿意當欲宥此囚死命。

translations.literal: He took the document presented yesterday, looked it over, and said to him, "You surely mean to spare this prisoner's life."
translations.idiomatic: He took up yesterday's petition, read it through, and said to him, "You mean to obtain a pardon for this man's life."

sentences.zh: 昨於齋坐見其事，亦有心活之。

translations.literal: Yesterday, seated in abstinence, I saw the matter and myself had a mind to let him live.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, while seated in abstinence, I saw the petition and was myself inclined to spare him.

sentences.zh: 但此囚罪重，不可全貸，既欲加恩，卿便當代任其罪。

translations.literal: But this prisoner's crime is grave and cannot be wholly remitted; since you wish to show favor, you must answer for his crime in his place.
translations.idiomatic: But this man's crime is grave and cannot be wholly forgiven; since you wish to show him favor, you must bear his guilt in his stead.

sentences.zh: 」因命左右收典籤付獄殺之，原此囚生命。

translations.literal: " He then ordered his attendants to seize the clerk, hand him over to prison, and put him to death, and pardoned the prisoner's life.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered his attendants to seize the clerk, commit him to prison, and execute him, while pardoning the prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其刑政如此，其下畏服，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: His administration of punishment was of this kind; those below feared and submitted, and none dared violate the prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his way with law and punishment; his subordinates feared and obeyed him, and none dared break the rules.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官，時年六十。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈征虜將軍，持節、監、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with Bearer of the Staff, supervision, and inspector's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with Bearer of the Staff, supervisory authority, and inspector's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 劉道產，彭城呂人，太尉諮議參軍簡之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Daochan was a native of Lü in Pengcheng, son of Jian, Advisory Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan came from Lü in Pengcheng; he was the son of Jian, who had served as advisory staff officer to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 簡之事在弟子康祖傳。

translations.literal: Jian's career is recorded in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's career is treated in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.

sentences.zh: 道產初為輔國參軍，無錫令，在縣有能名。

translations.literal: Daochan at first was Staff Officer Who Supports the State and Magistrate of Wuxi; in the county he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan began as Staff Officer Who Supports the State and as magistrate of Wuxi, where he won a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 高祖版為中軍行參軍，又為道憐驃騎參軍，襲父爵晉安縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him by patent as Acting Staff Officer of the Central Army, then Staff Officer under Daolian's Rapid Cavalry command; he inherited his father's fifth-rank noble title of Marquis of Jin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed him by patent as acting staff officer of the central army and then as staff officer on Daolian's Rapid Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.

sentences.zh: 廣州群盜因刺史謝道欣死為寇，攻沒州城，道憐加道產振武將軍南討，會始興謙之已平廣州，道產未至而反。

translations.literal: Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, became raiders and stormed the provincial capital; Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells the Martial and sent him south to attack, but by then Shizhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, and Daochan turned back before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: When the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin emboldened the bandit gangs of Guangzhou to raid and seize the provincial capital, Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells the Martial and sent him south on campaign; Shizhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, however, and Daochan turned back before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 元年，除寧遠將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of his reign he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the reign he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and grand administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 郡人黃公生、任肅之、張石之等竝譙縱餘燼，與姻親侯攬、羅奧等招引白水氐，規欲為亂。

translations.literal: Natives of the commandery Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others were all embers left from Qiao Zong's rebellion; with kinsmen by marriage Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they recruited the Baishui Di and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Local men Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others were remnants of Qiao Zong's revolt; with affinal kin Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they drew in the Baishui Di and plotted an uprising.

sentences.zh: 道產誅公生等二十一家，宥其餘黨。

translations.literal: Daochan executed Gongsheng and twenty other families and pardoned the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan put Gongsheng and twenty other families to death and pardoned the remaining conspirators.

sentences.zh: 還為彭城王義康驃騎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Central Army Staff Officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff of Prince of Pengcheng Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to serve as central army staff officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff of Prince Yikang of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，督梁、南秦二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he supervised military affairs in Liang and Nanqin provinces as General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3 (426) he was made supervisor of military affairs in Liang and Nanqin provinces, General of Distant Pacification, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 在州有惠化，關中流民，前後出漢川歸之者甚多。

translations.literal: In the province he showed benevolent governance; refugees from Guanzhong who came out along the Han to submit to him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he governed with benevolence, and many refugees from Guanzhong came out along the Han to submit to him.

sentences.zh: 六年，道產表置隴西、宋康二郡以領之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Daochan memorialized to establish the two commanderies of Longxi and Songkang to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Daochan memorialized to establish Longxi and Songkang commanderies to take charge of them.

sentences.zh: 七年，徵為後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to court as General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled to court as General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷竟陵王義宣左將軍諮議參軍，仍為持節、督雍、梁、南秦三州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Advisory Staff Officer to the Left General under Prince of Jingling Yixuan, and at the same time made Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and Nanqin provinces and the six commanderies of Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui in Jing Province, General of Distant Pacification, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong Province, and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became advisory staff officer to the left general under Prince Yixuan of Jingling and was also appointed Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and Nanqin provinces and six Jing commanderies (Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui), General of Distant Pacification, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong Province, and grand administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 善於臨民，在雍部政績尤著，蠻夷前後叛戾不受化者，竝皆順服，悉出緣沔為居。

translations.literal: Skilled in governing the people, his administrative achievements in the Yong region were especially notable; barbarians who had earlier rebelled and refused civilization all submitted, and all came out to settle along the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at governing the people, and his achievements in the Yong region were especially notable; tribes that had rebelled and refused assimilation all submitted and moved out to settle along the Han.

sentences.zh: 百姓樂業，民戶豐贍，由此有《襄陽樂歌》，自道產始也。

translations.literal: The common people were content in their occupations and households were prosperous and ample; hence arose the "Songs of Joy from Xiangyang," beginning with Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: The people prospered in their work and households grew wealthy; from this came the "Songs of Joy from Xiangyang," which began with Daochan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒，追贈征虜將軍，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; posthumously he was given the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with the posthumous name Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Punishes the Barbarians, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 道產惠澤被於西土，及喪還，諸蠻皆備衰絰，號哭追送，至於沔口。

translations.literal: Daochan's benevolence extended over the western lands; when his coffin returned, all the barbarian peoples put on mourning dress, wailed, and escorted him as far as the mouth of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's kindness had spread through the western regions; when his coffin was borne home, the tribal peoples all donned mourning garb, wailed, and escorted him as far as the mouth of the Han.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季啟太祖曰：「故輔國將軍劉道產患背癰，疾遂不救。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Hengyang Yiji, reported to Emperor Wen: "The late General Who Supports the State Liu Daochan suffered from a carbuncle on the back; the illness proved beyond cure."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji of Hengyang, inspector of Jing Province, reported to Emperor Wen: "The late General Who Supports the State Liu Daochan suffered from a carbuncle on his back; the illness proved fatal."

sentences.zh: 道產自鎮漢南，境接凶寇，政績既著，威懷兼舉。

translations.literal: Since Daochan garrisoned the south of the Han, his territory bordered fierce enemies; his administrative achievements were already notable, and he combined authority with conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he held the south of the Han, his territory bordered hostile enemies; his governance was already distinguished, and he combined firm authority with winning hearts.

sentences.zh: 年時猶可，方宣其用，奄至殞沒，傷怨特深。

translations.literal: His years were still serviceable and he was just beginning to display his usefulness when he suddenly perished; grief and resentment are especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was still in his prime and only beginning to show what he could do when death came suddenly; the grief and resentment are especially keen.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖懷，愍惜兼至。

translations.literal: I bow before Your sagely heart, which combines pity and regret.
translations.idiomatic: I trust that Your Majesty's heart will feel both pity and deep regret.

sentences.zh: 」長子延孫，別有傳。

translations.literal: " His eldest son Yansun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yansun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟延熙，因延孫之廕，大明中，為司徒右長史，黃門郎，臨海、義興太守。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, benefiting from Yansun's hereditary privilege, in the Daming era served as Right Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of State, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and Grand Administrator of Linhai and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, benefiting from Yansun's hereditary privilege, in the Daming era served as right chief clerk to the Grand Minister of State, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and grand administrator of Linhai and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，與四方同反，伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he joined the rebellions in the four directions and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he joined the widespread rebellions and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 道產弟道錫，巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Daochan's younger brother Daoxi served as grand administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，為氐寇所攻，道錫保城退敵，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia he was attacked by Di raiders; Daoxi held the city and repelled the enemy, and Emperor Wen commended him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 18 (441) he was attacked by Di raiders; Daoxi held the city and drove them off, and Emperor Wen praised him.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「前者兵寇攻逼，邊情波駭，廣威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守劉道錫，將率文武，盡心固守，保全之績，厥效可書。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "When the military raiders pressed the attack earlier, the border was shaken with alarm; General of Broad Prestige and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong Liu Daoxi led civil and military officials in devoted defense of the city; the achievement of preserving it is worthy to be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "When enemy forces pressed the attack earlier, the border was thrown into alarm. Liu Daoxi, General of Broad Prestige and grand administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies, led his civil and military officers in a resolute defense of the city; his success in preserving it deserves to be recorded."

sentences.zh: 可冠軍。

translations.literal: " He may be made Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be promoted to Champion [General]."

sentences.zh: 諮議參軍、前建威將軍、晉壽太守申坦，孤城弱眾，厲志致果，死傷參半，壯氣不衰，雖力屈陷沒，在誠宜甄。

translations.literal: Advisory Staff Officer and former General Who Establishes Prestige and Grand Administrator of Jinshou Shen Tan, with a lone city and weak forces, steeled his will to achieve results; casualties were half his men yet his spirit did not flag; though strength failed and he was overrun, his loyalty deserves recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tan, advisory staff officer and former General Who Establishes Prestige and grand administrator of Jinshou, held a lone city with few troops yet fought with fierce resolve; half his men were killed or wounded, yet his spirit never broke; though overwhelmed in the end, his loyalty deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 可建威將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: " He may be made General Who Establishes Prestige and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made General Who Establishes Prestige and grand administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies."

sentences.zh: 」初，氐寇至，城內眾寡，道錫募吏民守城，復租布二十年。

translations.literal: " When the Di raiders first arrived, the forces in the city were few; Daoxi recruited officials and commoners to defend the city and remitted land tax and cloth levies for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di raiders first arrived, the garrison was weak; Daoxi recruited officials and townspeople to defend the city and promised a twenty-year remission of land tax and cloth levies.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，朝議：「賊雖攻城，一戰便走，聽依本要，於事為優。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the court debated: "Although the bandits attacked the city, they fled after a single battle; it would be best to honor the original promise."
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, the court debated the matter: "Although the enemy attacked the city, they fled after a single engagement; it would be best to honor the original promise."

sentences.zh: 」右衛將軍沈演之、丹陽尹羊玄保、後軍長史范曄竝謂：「宜隨功勞裁量，不可全用本誓，多者不得過十年。

translations.literal: " General of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi, Governor of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and Chief Clerk of the Rear Army Fan Ye all said: "Rewards should be scaled to merit; the original pledge cannot be applied in full—the maximum should not exceed ten years."
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi, governor of Danyang Yang Xuanbao, and chief clerk of the rear army Fan Ye all argued: "Relief should be scaled to actual merit; the full original pledge cannot be kept—the maximum remission should be ten years."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed this view.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted their view.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷揚烈將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to General Who Displays Martial Glory and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to General Who Displays Martial Glory and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，坐貪縱過度，自杖治中荀齊文垂死，乘輿出城行，與阿尼同載，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, for excessive greed and indulgence, he personally flogged his aide Qi Wen of Xun until near death, went out of the city in his carriage for a pleasure outing, and rode in the same cart with a Buddhist nun; he was impeached by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was impeached for gross greed and license: he had personally beaten his aide Qi Wen of Xun nearly to death, taken his carriage out of the city on pleasure outings, and ridden in the same cart with a Buddhist nun.

sentences.zh: 值赦，明年散徵。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened; the next year he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty intervened; the following year he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 又以赦後餘贓，收下廷尉，被宥病卒。

translations.literal: Again, for remaining corruption after the amnesty, he was handed over to the Minister of Justice; he was pardoned but died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was again charged with corruption remaining after the amnesty and handed over to the Minister of Justice; he was pardoned but died of illness.

sentences.zh: 杜驥，字度世，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ji, courtesy name Dushi, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, whose courtesy name was Dushi, came from Duling in Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖預，晉征南將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu was General Who Conquers the South in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu had served Jin as General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 曾祖耽，避難河西，因仕張氏。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi to escape turmoil and consequently served the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Dan had fled the turmoil to Hexi and entered the service of the Zhang regime.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平涼州，父祖始還關中。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather at last returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather at last returned to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 兄坦，頗涉史傳。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tan was well versed in historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tan was well read in historical writings.

sentences.zh: 高祖征長安，席捲隨從南還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned against Chang'an, they swept along in his train and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned against Chang'an, they swept along in his train and returned south with him.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，任遇甚厚，歷後軍將軍，龍驤將軍，青、冀二州刺史，南平王鑠右將軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, Tan received very generous appointments, serving as General of the Rear Army, General of the Dragon Cavalry, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Staff Officer to the Right General under Prince of Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era, Tan enjoyed exceptional favor, serving as General of the Rear Army, General of the Dragon Cavalry, inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and staff officer to the right general under Prince Shuo of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 晚度北人，朝廷常以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，每為清塗所隔，坦以此慨然。

translations.literal: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court always treated him as crude and uncouth; though his talent could have been employed, he was repeatedly blocked from the pure official track, and Tan was deeply aggrieved by this.
translations.idiomatic: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court always treated him as crude and backward; though his talents could have been used, he was repeatedly shut out of the elite career track, and Tan brooded bitterly over this.

sentences.zh: 嘗與太祖言及史籍，上曰：「金日磾忠孝淳深，漢朝莫及，恨今世無復如此輩人。

translations.literal: Once, speaking with Emperor Wen about historical records, the emperor said: "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial piety were pure and deep; the Han dynasty had none to match him—I regret that our age has no such men again."
translations.idiomatic: Once, in conversation with Emperor Wen about historical writings, the emperor said: "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial devotion were pure and profound; the Han had no one to equal him—I regret that our age has produced no one of that kind."

sentences.zh: 」坦曰：「日磾之美，誠如聖詔。

translations.literal: " Tan said: "Jin Midi's excellence is indeed as Your sagely words say."
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied: "Jin Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Majesty says."

sentences.zh: 假使生乎今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知。

translations.literal: Had he been born in the present age, he would have had no leisure beyond tending horses—how could he have won recognition?
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived in our day, he would have had no time for anything but tending horses—how could he ever have won notice?

sentences.zh: 」上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也。

translations.literal: " The emperor changed color and said: "Why do you measure the court so meanly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. "Why do you think so little of the court?" he said.

sentences.zh: 」坦曰：「請以臣言之。

translations.literal: " Tan said: "Allow me to speak from my own case."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Let me speak from my own case."

sentences.zh: 臣本中華高族，亡曾祖晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，世葉相承，不殞其舊。

translations.literal: I am originally of a lofty clan of the Central States; my late great-great-grandfather, when Jin fell into disorder, was driven to the Liang region, yet generation after generation our line continued without losing its standing.
translations.idiomatic: I come from a distinguished Central Plains family; my late great-great-grandfather, when Jin was torn by chaos, was driven to the Liang region, yet our line endured generation after generation without losing its standing.

sentences.zh: 直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。

translations.literal: Simply because I crossed south late, I have been set apart as crude and uncouth.
translations.idiomatic: Simply because I crossed south late, I have been dismissed as crude and backward.

sentences.zh: 日磾胡人，身為牧圉，便超入內侍，齒列名賢。

translations.literal: Jin Midi was a barbarian who served as a horse-herd yet was promoted straight into inner attendance and ranked among famous worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Midi was a foreigner who tended horses, yet he was promoted straight into the inner service and ranked among the celebrated worthies.

sentences.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。

translations.literal: Though the sage dynasty may again select talent, I fear it might not be possible for me.
translations.idiomatic: Though our sage dynasty may again promote talent, I fear it would not be possible for a man like me.

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 北土舊法，問疾必遣子弟。

translations.literal: By the old custom of the north, when inquiring after the sick one always sent one's sons or younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: By northern custom, when inquiring after someone's health one always sent a son or younger relative.

sentences.zh: 驥年十三，父使候同郡韋華。

translations.literal: Ji was thirteen when his father sent him to call on Wei Hua of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was thirteen, his father sent him to call on Wei Hua of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 華子玄有高名，見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Wei's son Xuan had a high reputation; seeing Ji he was struck by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Xuan enjoyed a high reputation; struck by the boy, he gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 桂陽公義真鎮長安，辟為州主簿，後為義真車騎行參軍，員外散騎侍郎，江夏王義恭撫軍刑獄參軍，尚書都官郎，長沙王義欣後軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Duke of Guiyang Yizhen garrisoned Chang'an, Ji was recruited as provincial chief clerk; later he served as Acting Staff Officer on Yizhen's Chariots and Cavalry staff, Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Criminal Affairs Staff Officer on the Pacification Army staff of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice, and Recording Staff Officer on the Rear Army staff of Prince of Changsha Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Yizhen of Guiyang garrisoned Chang'an, Ji was recruited as provincial chief clerk; he later served on Yizhen's chariots-and-cavalry staff, as Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, as criminal affairs staff officer on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's pacification army staff, as Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice, and as recording staff officer on Prince Yixin of Changsha's rear army staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，隨到彥之入河南，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was promoted to General Who Establishes Martial [Prestige].
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 7 (430) he followed Dao Yanzhi south of the Yellow River and was promoted to General Who Establishes Martial [Prestige].

sentences.zh: 索虜撤河南戍悉歸河北，彥之使驥守洛陽。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians withdrew all garrisons south of the Yellow River back north of the river; Yanzhi ordered Ji to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy withdrew all garrisons south of the Yellow River back to the north bank; Yanzhi ordered Ji to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 洛陽城不治既久，又無糧食，及彥之敗退，驥欲棄城走，慮為太祖所誅。

translations.literal: Luoyang had long gone unrepaired and had no provisions; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wished to abandon the city and flee but feared execution by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had long been neglected and had no provisions; when Yanzhi was beaten and forced to retreat, Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee but feared execution by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖平關洛，致鐘虡舊器南還，一大鐘墜洛水。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Gaozu pacified Guanzhong and Luoyang, he had the old bells and ritual vessels brought south; one great bell fell into the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu had pacified Guanzhong and Luoyang, he had the old bells and ritual vessels brought south; one great bell fell into the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 至是太祖遣將姚聳夫領千五百人迎致之。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wen sent the general Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to fetch and bring it back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen now sent the general Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.

sentences.zh: 時聳夫政率所領牽鐘于洛水，驥乃誑之曰：「虜既南渡，洛城勢弱，今修理城池，竝已堅固，軍糧又足，所乏者人耳。

translations.literal: At that time Songfu was just leading his men to haul the bell at the Luo River; Ji then deceived him, saying: "The barbarians have already crossed south; Luoyang is weak in strength—but we have now repaired the walls and they are all firm, military grain is ample, and all we lack is men."
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was then leading his men to haul the bell at the Luo River; Ji deceived him, saying: "The enemy has already crossed south, and Luoyang looks weak—but we have repaired the walls and they are now solid, our grain stores are full, and all we lack is manpower."

sentences.zh: 君率眾見就，共守此城，大功既立，取鐘無晚。

translations.literal: If you bring your forces to join us and we defend this city together, once the great achievement is secured, retrieving the bell will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Bring your men here and help us hold the city; once that great deed is done, there will be time enough to fetch the bell."

sentences.zh: 」聳夫信之，率所領就驥。

translations.literal: " Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.

sentences.zh: 既至，見城不可守，又無糧食，於是引眾去。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they saw the city could not be held and there was no food; they then led their troops away.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, they saw the city could not be held and there was no food, and so they led their troops away.

sentences.zh: 驥亦委城南奔，白太祖曰：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫及城便走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。

translations.literal: Ji also abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to Emperor Wen: "I had meant to defend to the death, but when Yao Songfu reached the city he fled at once; morale collapsed and could no longer be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to Emperor Wen: "I had intended to defend the city to the death, but when Yao Songfu arrived he fled at once; morale collapsed and could no longer be held."

sentences.zh: 」上大怒，使建威將軍鄭順之殺聳夫於壽陽。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 聳夫，吳興武康人。

translations.literal: Songfu was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 勇果有氣力，宋世偏裨小將莫及。

translations.literal: Brave, resolute, and strong, among the junior commanders of the Song age none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Brave, resolute, and powerful, no junior officer of the Song could match him.

sentences.zh: 始隨到彥之北伐，與虜遇，聳夫手斬托跋燾叔父英文特勒首，燾以馬百匹贖之。

translations.literal: At first he followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; encountering the barbarians, Songfu personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; in an encounter with the enemy, Songfu personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 以驥為通直郎，射聲校尉，世祖征虜諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Ji was appointed Direct Attendant, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, and Advisory Staff Officer on the expeditionary staff of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was appointed Direct Attendant, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, and advisory staff officer on Emperor Xiaowu's expeditionary staff.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出督青、冀二州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces and the two commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an in Xu Province as General of Distant Pacification and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was sent out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces and Dongguan and Dong'an commanderies in Xu Province as General of Distant Pacification and inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 在任八年，惠化著於齊土。

translations.literal: During eight years in office his benevolent governance was notable throughout the Qi region.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years in office his benevolent rule was renowned throughout the Qi region.

sentences.zh: 自義熙至於宋末，刺史唯羊穆之及驥，為吏民所稱詠。

translations.literal: From the Yixi era to the end of Song, among inspectors only Yang Muzhi and Ji were praised and celebrated by officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yixi era to the end of Song, among provincial inspectors only Yang Muzhi and Ji were praised and celebrated by officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徵左軍將軍，兄坦代為刺史，北土以為榮焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan replaced him as inspector, and northerners regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan replaced him as provincial inspector, and northerners took this as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 坦長子琬為員外散騎侍郎，太祖嘗有函詔敕坦，琬輒開視。

translations.literal: Tan's eldest son Wan was Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry; Emperor Wen once had a sealed edict instructing Tan, and Wan promptly opened and read it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's eldest son Wan served as Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry; Emperor Wen once sent Tan a sealed edict, and Wan promptly opened and read it.

sentences.zh: 信未發又追取之，敕函已發，大相推檢。

translations.literal: Before the letter was sent a recall was issued, but the sealed packet had already gone out, and a major investigation followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the letter could be dispatched a recall was issued, but the sealed packet had already been sent, and a major investigation followed.

sentences.zh: 丞都答云：「諸郎開視。

translations.literal: The aides all answered: "The young masters opened and read it."
translations.idiomatic: The aides all answered: "The young masters opened and read it."

sentences.zh: 」上遣主書詰責，驥答曰：「開函是臣第四子季文，伏待刑坐。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent a chief clerk to question and rebuke him; Ji replied: "The one who opened the packet was my fourth son Jiwen; he awaits punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a chief clerk to question him; Ji replied: "The one who opened the packet was my fourth son Jiwen; he awaits punishment."

sentences.zh: 」上特原不問。

translations.literal: " The emperor specially pardoned him and took no further action.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 長子長文，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Changwen died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Changwen died young.

sentences.zh: 第五子幼文，薄於行。

translations.literal: His fifth son Youwen was deficient in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth son Youwen was morally deficient.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，以軍功為驍騎將軍，封邵陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, for military merit he was made General of Valiant Cavalry and enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made General of Valiant Cavalry for military merit and enfeoffed as Baron of Shaoyang County with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋坐巧佞奪爵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for craftiness and flattery, his noble rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his noble rank was stripped for craftiness and flattery.

sentences.zh: 後以發太尉廬江王禕謀反事，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, for exposing the rebellion plot of Grand Marshal Prince of Lujiang Yi, he was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for exposing the rebellion plot of Grand Marshal Prince Yi of Lujiang, he was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為輔國將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Supports the State and inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元徽中，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Under the deposed emperor in the Yuanhui era he was Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor in the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 幼文所蒞貪橫，家累千金，女伎數十人，絲竹晝夜不絕，與沈勃、孫超之居止接近，常相從，又竝與阮佃夫厚善。

translations.literal: In every post Youwen held he was greedy and overbearing; his household amassed wealth of a thousand gold, he kept dozens of female performers, and string and wind music never ceased day or night; he lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and constantly kept their company, and was also on close terms with Ruan Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held Youwen was greedy and overbearing; his household amassed great wealth, he kept dozens of female performers, and music never ceased day or night; he lived near Shen Bo and Sun Chaozhi and constantly kept their company, and was also close to Ruan Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 佃夫死，廢帝深疾之。

translations.literal: When Tianfu died, the deposed emperor deeply resented them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu died, the deposed emperor came to resent them deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝微行夜出，輒在幼文門牆之間，聽其弦管，積久轉不能平，於是自率宿衛兵誅幼文、勃、超之等。

translations.literal: The emperor would go out incognito at night and linger by Youwen's gate and walls to listen to his string music; as this went on he grew ever less able to bear it, and at last personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would slip out at night and linger by Youwen's gate to listen to his music; as this went on his resentment grew until at last he personally led the palace guard to execute Youwen, Bo, Chaozhi, and the others.

sentences.zh: 幼文兄叔文為長水校尉，及諸子侄在京邑方鎮者竝誅。

translations.literal: Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was Colonel of the Long River; all sons, nephews, and kin in the capital or in provincial posts were likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen's elder brother Shuwen, who was Colonel of the Long River, and all sons, nephews, and kin in the capital or in provincial posts were likewise executed.

sentences.zh: 唯幼文兄季文、弟希文等數人，逃亡得免。

translations.literal: Only Youwen's elder brother Jiwen, younger brother Xiwen, and a few others escaped by flight.
translations.idiomatic: Only Youwen's elder brother Jiwen, younger brother Xiwen, and a few others escaped by fleeing.

sentences.zh: 申恬，字公休，魏郡魏人也。

translations.literal: Shen Tian, courtesy name Gongxiu, was a native of Wei in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tian, whose courtesy name was Gongxiu, came from Wei in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鍾，為石虎司徒。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Zhong was Grand Minister of State under Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Zhong had served Shi Hu as Grand Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 高祖平廣固，恬父宣、宣從父兄永皆得歸國，竝以幹用見知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's paternal cousin Yong were both able to return to the realm and were known for their competence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's paternal cousin Yong were both able to return to the realm and were recognized for their competence.

sentences.zh: 永歷青、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong served as Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yong served as inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 宣，太祖元嘉初，亦歷兗、青二州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan, at the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, at the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as inspector of Yan and Qing provinces.

sentences.zh: 恬兄謨，與朱脩之守滑臺，為虜所沒，後得叛還。

translations.literal: Tian's elder brother Mo, together with Zhu Xiuzhi, defended Huatai and was captured by the barbarians, but later defected and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's elder brother Mo had defended Huatai together with Zhu Xiuzhi, was captured by the enemy, and later defected back to the Song.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he was Grand Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era he served as grand administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 恬初為驃騎道憐長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Tian at first was Acting Staff Officer on the long-term staff of Daolian's Rapid Cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: Tian began as acting staff officer on the long-term staff of Daolian's Rapid Cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜東宮殿中將軍，度還臺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace General of the Eastern Palace and then transferred back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace General of the Eastern Palace and then transferred back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 直省十載，不請休息。

translations.literal: He served on palace duty for ten years without requesting leave.
translations.idiomatic: He served on palace duty for ten years without ever requesting leave.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，出為綏遠將軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and grand administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 轉在北海，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Beihai and promoted to General of Distant Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Beihai and promoted to General of Distant Pacification.

sentences.zh: 所至皆有政績。

translations.literal: Everywhere he went he achieved administrative success.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he achieved notable administrative success.

sentences.zh: 又為北譙、梁二郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He again served as Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Beiqiao and Liang, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as grand administrator of Beiqiao and Liang commanderies, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 郡境邊接任榛，屢被寇抄。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered on Ren Zhen's territory and was repeatedly raided.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery bordered the territory of the outlaw Ren Zhen and was repeatedly raided.

sentences.zh: 恬到，密知賊來，仍伏兵要害，出其不意，悉皆禽殄。

translations.literal: When Tian arrived he secretly learned the bandits were coming, then laid troops in ambush at a critical point and, taking them by surprise, captured and destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian arrived he learned secretly that the raiders were coming, laid troops in ambush at a critical point, and taking them by surprise captured and destroyed them all.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，遷督魯、東平、濟北三郡軍事、泰山太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to supervise military affairs in the three commanderies of Lu, Dongping, and Jibei as Grand Administrator of Taishan, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 12 (435) he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Lu, Dongping, and Jibei commanderies as grand administrator of Taishan, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 惠威兼著，吏民便之。

translations.literal: His benevolence and authority were both notable, and officials and commoners found him a convenience.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence and authority were both notable, and officials and commoners alike benefited from his rule.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶鎮江陵，為平西中兵參軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linchuan Yiqing garrisoned Jiangling, he served as Central Army Staff Officer of the Pacification of the West and Grand Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yiqing of Linchuan garrisoned Jiangling, he served as central army staff officer of the Pacification of the West and grand administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季代義慶，又度安西府，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, he again crossed to the Pacification of the West headquarters and was promoted to General of Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yiji of Hengyang replaced Yiqing, he again transferred to the Pacification of the West headquarters and was promoted to General of Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子屯騎校尉，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the Heir Apparent, then left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the Heir Apparent, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，冀州移鎮歷下，以恬督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、揚烈將軍、冀州刺史，明年，加濟南太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Ji garrison was moved to Lixia; Tian was made supervisor of military affairs in Ji Province and the three commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan in Qing Province, General Who Displays Martial Glory, and Inspector of Ji Province; the next year he was also given Jinan as grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Ji garrison was moved to Lixia; Tian was made supervisor of military affairs in Ji Province and Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan commanderies in Qing Province, General Who Displays Martial Glory, and inspector of Ji Province; the following year he was also made grand administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 時又遷換諸郡守，恬上表曰：「伏聞朝恩當加臣濟南太守，仰惟優旨，荒心散越。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a general rotation of commandery administrators; Tian submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that the court's grace will add to me the post of Grand Administrator of Jinan; looking up at this excellent decree, my unsettled heart is scattered and overwhelmed."
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was also a general rotation of commandery administrators; Tian submitted a memorial saying: "I have learned that the court intends to add the post of grand administrator of Jinan to my duties; at this gracious decree my unsettled heart is overwhelmed with gratitude."

sentences.zh: 臣殃咎之餘，遭蒙逾忝，寵私罔己，復兼今授，豈其愚迷，所能上答。

translations.literal: I am one who remains after calamity and fault, yet have received favor beyond my deserts; private grace has known no limit, and now this additional appointment—how could my foolish blindness possibly repay it?
translations.idiomatic: I am one who survives after calamity and fault, yet have received favor beyond my deserts; private grace has known no limit, and now this additional appointment—how could my dull wits possibly repay it?

sentences.zh: 臣近至止，即履行所統，究其形宜。

translations.literal: Since I recently arrived and took up my post, I have at once toured the territory under my command and examined its strategic conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Since I recently arrived and took up my post, I have at once toured the territory under my command and examined its strategic conditions.

sentences.zh: 河、濟之間，應置戍捍，其中四處，急須修立，甕口故城，又是要所，宜移太原，委以邊事。

translations.literal: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers garrisons ought to be established for defense; of these four sites urgently need to be built up, and the old city at Wengkou is again a critical point—Taiyuan should be moved there and entrusted with border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yellow and Ji rivers defensive garrisons ought to be established; four sites urgently need to be built up, and the old city at Wengkou is again a critical point—Taiyuan commandery should be moved there and entrusted with border affairs.

sentences.zh: 緣山諸邏，並得除省，防衛綏懷，利便非一。

translations.literal: The various outposts along the mountains could all be abolished and streamlined; defense, pacification, and reassurance would gain more than one advantage.
translations.idiomatic: The various mountain outposts could all be abolished and streamlined; defense, pacification, and reassurance would gain more than one advantage.

sentences.zh: 呂綽誠效益著，深同臣意，百姓聞者，咸皆附說，急有同異，二三未宜。

translations.literal: Lu Chuo's loyal effectiveness is notable and deeply accords with my view; common people who hear of it all attach themselves to the proposal—only on urgent points of agreement and difference two or three matters are not yet suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chuo's loyal effectiveness is notable and deeply accords with my view; common people who hear of it all support the proposal—only on two or three urgent points of disagreement are matters not yet suitable.

sentences.zh: 但房紹之蒞郡經年，軍民粗狎，改以帶臣，有乖永事。

translations.literal: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years and army and people have grown somewhat familiar with him; to change and attach me instead runs counter to lasting arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: But Fang Shaozhi has governed the commandery for years and army and people have grown accustomed to him; to replace him with me runs counter to stable administration.

sentences.zh: 遠牽太原，於民為苦。

translations.literal: Dragging Taiyuan far away would be a hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Taiyuan far away would be a hardship for the people.

sentences.zh: 而甕口之計，復成交互，人情非樂，容有不安。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wengkou plan would again create mutual entanglement; popular feeling would not be pleased, and there might be unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Wengkou plan would again create mutual complications; popular feeling would not welcome it, and unrest might follow.

sentences.zh: 疆場威刑，患不開廣，若得依先處分，公私允緝。

translations.literal: On the frontier authority and punishment fear that scope is not broad enough; if we can follow the prior disposition, public and private interests will both be well ordered."
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, authority and punishment need room to operate; if we can follow the prior disposition, public and private interests will both be well ordered."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 詔有司曰：「恬所陳當是事宜，近諸除授可悉停。」

translations.literal: An edict to the relevant offices said: "What Tian stated accords with what is fitting; recent appointments may all be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the relevant offices said: "What Tian stated is appropriate; recent appointments may all be suspended."

sentences.zh: 北虜入寇，恬摧擊之，為虜所破，被徴還都。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded, Tian struck at them but was defeated by the barbarians and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern enemy invaded, Tian attacked them but was defeated and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，起為通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled to serve as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled to serve as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 是歲，索虜南寇，其武昌王向青州。

translations.literal: That year the northern barbarians raided south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year the northern enemy raided south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 遣恬援東陽，因與輔國司馬、齊郡太守龐秀之保城固守。

translations.literal: Tian was sent to reinforce Dongyang and, together with the Pacification Army Staff Officer and Grand Administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi, held the city in stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was sent to reinforce Dongyang and, together with the pacification army staff officer and grand administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi, held the city in stout defense.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣青州別駕解榮之率垣護之還援恬等，仍傍南山得入。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent Qing Province Vice-Prefect Xie Rongzhi to lead Yuan Huzhi back to relieve Tian and the others; they entered by way along the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin sent Qing Province vice-prefect Xie Rongzhi to lead Yuan Huzhi back to relieve Tian and the others; they entered along the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊朝來脅城，日晚輒退。

translations.literal: The bandits came each morning to threaten the city and each evening withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came each morning to threaten the city and each evening withdrew.

sentences.zh: 城內乃出車北門外，環塹為營，欲挑戰，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Those inside the city then sent chariots outside the north gate, ringed the moat to make a camp, and sought battle; the bandits did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders then sent chariots outside the north gate, ringed the moat to form a camp, and sought battle; the enemy did not dare press close.

sentences.zh: 停五日，東過抄略清河郡及驛道南數千家，從東安、東莞出下邳。

translations.literal: After five days' halt they passed east, raiding Qinghe commandery and several thousand households south of the post road, and left through Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: After five days they passed east, raiding Qinghe commandery and several thousand households south of the post road, and left through Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 下邳太守垣閬閉城距守，保全二千餘家。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Xiapi Yuan Lang closed the city and resisted, preserving more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand administrator of Xiapi Yuan Lang closed the city and resisted, preserving more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 虜退，以恬為寧朔將軍、山陽太守。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, Tian was made General of Pacifying the North and Grand Administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, Tian was made General of Pacifying the North and grand administrator of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 善於治民，所蒞有績。

translations.literal: Skilled in governing the people, in every post he held he achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at governing the people, he achieved results in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，遷青州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was transferred to Inspector of Qing Province, with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was transferred to inspector of Qing Province, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋加督徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was also given supervision of military affairs in the two commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also given supervision of military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an commanderies in Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，又督冀州。

translations.literal: The next year he also supervised Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he also supervised Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 齊地連歲興兵，百姓凋弊，恬初防衛邊境，勸課農桑，二三年間，遂皆優實。

translations.literal: The Qi region had raised armies year after year and the common people were depleted; when Tian first defended the border he urged agriculture and sericulture, and within two or three years all became prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi region had raised armies year after year and the people were depleted; when Tian first defended the border he urged agriculture and sericulture, and within two or three years all became prosperous and secure.

sentences.zh: 性清約，頻處州郡，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal; though he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts, his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold, and the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was pure and frugal; though he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts, his wife and children still knew hunger and cold, and the age praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，遷督豫州軍事、寧朔將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yu Province as General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2 (455) he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yu Province as General of Pacifying the North and inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，疾病徵還，於道卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: The next year, ill, he was summoned back and died on the road at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, ill, he was recalled and died on the road, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無遺財。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no property left.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death his household had no property left.

sentences.zh: 子實，南譙郡太守，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi was Grand Administrator of Nanqiao commandery and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi served as grand administrator of Nanqiao commandery and died young.

sentences.zh: 謨子元嗣，海陵、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Mo's son Yuansi was Grand Administrator of Hailing and Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son Yuansi served as grand administrator of Hailing and Guangling.

sentences.zh: 元嗣弟謙，太始初，以軍功歷軍校，官至輔國將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the beginning of Taishi, for military merit rose through army command posts to General Who Supports the State and Interior Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the beginning of Taishi, rose through army command posts for military merit to General Who Supports the State and interior administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 永子坦，自巴西、梓潼遷梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，為世祖鎮軍諮議參軍，與王玄謨圍滑臺不克，免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was Advisory Staff Officer on Emperor Xiaowu's Pacification Army staff; with Wang Xuanmo he besieged Huatai without success and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 26 (449) he was advisory staff officer on Emperor Xiaowu's pacification army staff; with Wang Xuanmo he besieged Huatai without success and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板行建威將軍、濟南、平原二郡太守，復攻確磝，敗退，下歷城。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qing Province Xiao Bin appointed him by patent as Acting General Who Establishes Prestige and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Jinan and Pingyuan; he again attacked Que'ao, was defeated and withdrew, and descended to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Qing Province Xiao Bin appointed him by patent as acting General Who Establishes Prestige and grand administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan commanderies; he again attacked Que'ao, was defeated and withdrew, and fell back to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話起義討元兇，假坦輔國將軍，為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Xiao Sihua raised forces to punish the arch-criminal, Tan was given acting rank as General Who Supports the State and served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Sihua raised forces to punish the usurper, Tan was given acting rank as General Who Supports the State and served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為太子右衛率，寧朔將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, General of Pacifying the North, and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was right commandant of the heir apparent's guard, General of Pacifying the North, and inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，虜寇兗州，世祖遣太子衛率薛安都、新除東陽太守沈法系北討，至兗州，虜已去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming the barbarians raided Yan Province; Emperor Xiaowu sent the Heir Apparent's Guard Commandant Xue Andu and the newly appointed Grand Administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxi on a northern campaign; when they reached Yan Province the barbarians had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 (457) the enemy raided Yan Province; Emperor Xiaowu sent the heir apparent's guard commandant Xue Andu and the newly appointed grand administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxi on a northern campaign; when they reached Yan Province the enemy had already gone.

sentences.zh: 坦建議：「任榛亡命，屢犯邊民，軍出無功，宜因此翦撲。

translations.literal: Tan proposed: "The outlaw Ren Zhen has repeatedly violated border peoples; the army went out without success—we ought to take this opportunity to cut him down."
translations.idiomatic: Tan proposed: "The outlaw Ren Zhen has repeatedly raided border peoples; the campaign achieved nothing—we ought to take this opportunity to destroy him."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 亡命先已聞知，舉村逃走，安都與法系坐白衣領職，坦棄市。

translations.literal: The outlaw had already heard in advance; whole villages fled. Andu and Faxi were punished by serving in plain clothes while retaining office; Tan was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw had already heard in advance; whole villages fled. Andu and Faxi were punished by serving in plain clothes while retaining office; Tan was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 群臣為之請，莫能得。

translations.literal: The ministers all pleaded for him but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all pleaded for him but could not save him.

sentences.zh: 將行刑，始興公沈慶之入市抱坦慟哭曰：「卿無罪，為朝廷所枉誅，我入市亦當不久。

translations.literal: As the execution was about to be carried out, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the marketplace, embraced Tan, and wept aloud: "You are guiltless and are being wrongly put to death by the court; my entry into the marketplace will not be long either."
translations.idiomatic: As the execution was about to be carried out, Duke Qingzhi of Shixing entered the marketplace, embraced Tan, and wept aloud: "You are innocent and are being wrongly put to death by the court; I too will not be long in joining you here."

sentences.zh: 」市官以白上，乃原生命，繫尚方。

translations.literal: " The marketplace officer reported this to the emperor, who then spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: The marketplace officer reported this to the emperor, who then spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 尋被宥，復為驍騎將軍，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned, again made General of Valiant Cavalry, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pardoned, again made General of Valiant Cavalry, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子令孫，前廢帝景和中，為永嘉王子仁左軍司馬、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, was Left Army Staff Officer to Prince Ziren of Yongjia and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, was left army staff officer to Prince Ziren of Yongjia and grand administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，討薛安都。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen made him General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of Xu Province to campaign against Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen made him General of Pacifying the North and inspector of Xu Province to campaign against Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 行至淮陽，即與安都合。

translations.literal: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.

sentences.zh: 弟闡，時為濟陰太守，戍睢陵城，奉順不同安都，安都攻圍不能克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chan was then Grand Administrator of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he submitted to the court and would not follow Andu, and Andu besieged him without being able to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chan was then grand administrator of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he remained loyal to the court and would not follow Andu, and Andu besieged him without being able to take the city.

sentences.zh: 會令孫至，遣往睢陵令說闡降，闡既降，殺之，令孫亦見殺。

translations.literal: When Lingsun arrived he sent someone to Suiling to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan had surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingsun arrived he sent someone to Suiling to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan had surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was also killed.

sentences.zh: 先是，清河崔諲亦以將吏見知高祖，永初末，為振威將軍、東萊太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe was also known to Emperor Gaozu as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Displays Martial Prestige and Grand Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe was also known to Emperor Gaozu as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Displays Martial Prestige and grand administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，亡命司馬靈期、司馬順之千餘人圍東萊，諲擊之，斬靈期等三十級。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the brief reign, more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the brief reign, more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，至青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen he rose to Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen he rose to inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢之良吏，居官者或長子孫，孫、曹之世，善職者亦二三十載，皆敷政以盡民和，興讓以存簡久。

translations.literal: The historian says: Among the good officials of Han, some held office long enough to see their sons and grandsons grow up; in the ages of Sun and Cao, capable administrators also served twenty or thirty years, all spreading governance to achieve popular harmony and promoting yielding to preserve simplicity and endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Among the good officials of Han, some held office long enough to see their sons and grandsons grow up; in the ages of Sun and Cao, capable administrators also served twenty or thirty years, all spreading good governance to achieve popular harmony and promoting yielding to preserve simplicity and endurance.

sentences.zh: 及晚代風烈漸衰，非才有起伏，蓋所遭之時異也。

translations.literal: By the late age moral force gradually declined; it was not that talent rose and fell, but rather that the times they encountered differed.
translations.idiomatic: By the late age moral force gradually declined; it was not that talent rose and fell, but that the times men encountered differed.

sentences.zh: 劉道產之在漢南，歷年逾十，惠化流於樊沔，頗有前世遺風，故能樹績垂名，斯為美矣！

translations.literal: Liu Daochan's tenure south of the Han lasted more than ten years; his benevolent governance flowed through Fan and Mian, bearing much of the legacy style of earlier ages—thus he could establish achievement and leave a lasting name; this is truly admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan held the south of the Han for more than ten years; his benevolent rule spread through Fan and Mian, bearing much of the style of earlier ages—thus he could establish lasting achievement and leave a celebrated name. This is truly admirable!
